catalysts.headline: PG&E's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reiterates an aggregate Kincade Fire liability of $1.325 billion (before available insurance), unchanged since 2025-12-31 and still unchanged as of 2026-09-30; the company continues to record estimated wildfire liabilities at the low end of the reasonably estimable range of losses and says actual losses could be higher as claims develop. The filing also notes that the statutes of limitations for federal fire-suppression claims tied to the 2021 Dixie Fire and 2022 Mosquito Fire expire in 2027 and 2028 respectively, and that PG&E intends to contest both criminal charges and civil complaints (inverse condemnation, negligence, and other theories) tied to its wildfire litigation.
catalysts.impact: No new liability quantification; reiterates existing Kincade Fire exposure and flags upcoming statute-of-limitations deadlines on older fires
catalysts.note: Date reflects the 10-Q's reporting period (2026-09-30); exact SEC filing date not independently confirmed this session. This is additional detail from the same Q3 2026 filing already partly on file (which only captured the Q3 earnings print itself).
